formNote: Mojidata IDS: ⿱耂子. The Shuowen: 孝，善事父母者。从老省，从子，子承老也 — “one who serves parents well: from 老 abbreviated and 子; the child bearing up the old.”
summary: Devotion to parents: graphically a child under an elder, holding them up. Confucians made it the root of humaneness and the model for loyalty.
placement: On the rising side of the fold, between 仁 below and 德 above. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: The Child Bearing Up the Old
satellites.evidence: 孝 is 耂 over 子 (Mojidata IDS). The Shuowen reads it as 子承老也, “the child bearing up the old”: the graph puts the child beneath the elder, carrying them.

satellites.title: Piety Toward Those Who Came Before
satellites.evidence: English renders 孝 as “filial piety”, borrowing Latin pietas, the dutiful devotion a Roman owed to parents, country and gods. Both words make care for those who came before a virtue in its own right, not only a feeling.
satellites.caveat: Pietas reached past the family to the gods and the state; 孝 centres on parents and ancestors, and Confucians modelled loyalty on it rather than the reverse. The likeness is in the shape of the virtue, not in its doctrine.
